own_solution.law: For rolling without slipping on stationary ground, v_CM = omega R = (12.0)(0.5) = 6 m/s. With slipping permitted, angular speed and radius do not determine the center-of-mass speed.
assumptions: Obtaining 6 m/s requires rolling without slipping, which the problem does not state.

defect_reasons.missing_assumption: All four variants omit the rolling-without-slipping condition required to infer center-of-mass speed from angular speed and radius.

counterexamples: A wheel with radius 0.5 m and angular speed 12.0 rad/s can move along stationary ground at 3 m/s while slipping.
The same wheel can instead move at 8 m/s while slipping, satisfying the stated conditions with a different center-of-mass speed.
notes: No unique numerical answer exists in any variant. Each conveyor-belt statement is structurally disconnected (D), so changing its speed does not resolve the missing rolling condition. The legacy renderings differ only in the belt speed, consistently expressed in m/s.
